title: The long story
hookLine: a year of people: the Prophet ﷺ, those who walked beside him, and those who came after

lines: A BOOK DOESN'T WALK ON ITS OWN.
cards: A book doesn't walk from one century to the next on its own. Someone memorized it. Someone recited it at dawn to a half-asleep child.
Someone copied it, taught it, argued over it, carried it on a camel or in a coat pocket. For two years this path has listened to the Qur'an itself, surah by surah.
This year turns to the people standing next to it: the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the ones who walked beside him, and the long line who came after. Today's word is the shape of that year.

teach.h: SIRAH: THE STORY OF A LIFE.
teach.b: Muslims have a word for the story of the Prophet's life: sirah. One of the early lives that comes down to us was put together by Ibn Ishaq, and it reaches us largely through a later editor, Ibn Hisham.
Then there are the companions, the sahabah. The Qur'an remembers one of them without giving his name.

teach.h: THE SECOND OF TWO, IN THE CAVE.
teach.b: In surah nine it describes the Prophet hiding in a cave on his escape from Mecca, and Pickthall's translation reads: "the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us."
Commentators identify that comrade as Abu Bakr. A whole friendship, inside one verse. Then the ones after.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet is reported to say that the best people are his own generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.
A hadith comes with its isnad, the chain of names attached to it: this one heard it from that one, who heard it from another. Every saying arrives holding someone's hand. So here is this year's rule.
The Qur'an and the major hadith collections come first. The sirah adds color and detail, and where a story is told only by later writers, or told different ways, this path will say so out loud.
And the people will be people: brave, frightened, generous, sometimes wrong. The Qur'an calls the Messenger a good example.

teach.h: GRIEVE NOT. LO! ALLAH IS WITH US.
teach.b: The people around him show what following it looked like up close: a frightened friend in a cave, being told not to grieve.

how: Sirah books and mosque classes teach the life of the Prophet ﷺ alongside the Qur'an, and Muslims pray, in words from surah fifty-nine, for forgiveness for those who came before them in faith.

games.q: at a dinner, someone tells a moving story about the Prophet ﷺ you've never heard. how does this path handle a story like that this year?
o: tell it as certain, because it's beautiful.
say where it comes from: Qur'an and major hadith first, later stories flagged.
leave out every story that isn't in the Qur'an.
games.why: the Qur'an and the major hadith collections come first; the sirah adds detail, and when a story is told only later, or told different ways, the path says so.

practice: Bring to mind one person from history you admire, well-known or not: a scholar, a great-grandmother, a companion whose story you half remember, and ask what they carried that reached you, a skill, a book, a kind of courage.
If you pray, you can ask Allah's mercy for them; if you don't, simply stay with them, and notice that it came this far because they carried it.

wordCard.voice: Sirah. The story of the Prophet's life ﷺ, carried through companions and the generations after, each handing it to the next. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the life story of the Prophet ﷺ.
